key_insight: Blindly ‘tokenmaxxing’—pursuing ever-larger context windows and agentic behavior—is not the right default. Sensible, constrained deployments that match model capabilities to real-world needs yield better safety, cost-efficiency, and reliability.
problem_solved: Counters the current race to embed agentic/long-context AI into every workflow by diagnosing the harms (cost, latency, brittleness, hallucinations, governance gaps) and offering a practical alternative for responsible deployment.
method: Diagnose the problem with conceptual analysis and illustrative case examples showing diminishing returns and failure modes as token/context use and agentic complexity grow.
Propose a deployment framework/checklist: assess necessity of extended context or agency, prefer simpler/specialized models when adequate, require human oversight and explicit constraints.
Recommend operational metrics and monitoring: marginal utility per token, cost/latency trade-offs, failure-mode tracking, and guardrails for emergent behaviors.
impact: Gives AI/ML practitioners a pragmatic playbook to avoid wasteful or risky designs, enabling more trustworthy, cost-effective systems by prioritizing fit-for-purpose models, constraints, and active monitoring.
visual_elements: Diminishing-returns curve: performance gain vs. number of tokens/context length

paper_title: Stop ‘tokenmaxxing’ and deploy AI sensibly instead
